title: Glossary term
description: One sense of one word the workbench shows a reader, written for a practitioner. Every tooltip, page head, rail description, palette line, plate key and edge caption reads one of these records; the app writes no definition of its own. A record is either SOURCED -- its `sources` already sit, character for character, in a corpus bibliography -- or EDITORIAL, in which case its `basis` names the file it read and quotes it verbatim. Editorial is a licence to explain, never a licence to invent, and build/check_glossary.py holds every basis to the file it names. One file per term at glossary/<id>.json; the authoring rules are glossary/README.md.

id.description: One sense per id, and the filename (glossary/<id>.json). Never reused: a wrong id is superseded, not renamed. A word with two senses is two records with two ids.

term.description: The words the reader meets, exactly as the screen shows them. A rail label, a dossier section label and a page eyebrow ARE this string, not a second spelling of it.

family.description: The group the Glossary page lists the term under, in this order. Families surface, section, nav-group, layer and judgment require the id prefix `<family>-`; a record that binds an enum value takes the family of the field it binds.

definition.description: Plain, in a practitioner's register, never addressed to an AI agent. At most forty-five words (the checker counts). No digits, no counts, no build history, no work-package or question numbers, no snake_case identifiers: a definition must still be true when every number in the repository has changed.

kind.description: `sourced` requires `sources` and forbids `basis`; `editorial` the reverse. The glossary's own word is not a glossary term: `param-kind-editorial` names a different thing, a kind of kit parameter.

sources.description: Published works this definition rests on. Each string must already appear verbatim as an item of a `sources` list in some record under styles/, faults/, rooms/, proportions/, groupings/ or partis/. The glossary never introduces a source the corpus does not already cite: that is the no-invented-source guard.

basis.description: For an editorial record: the file or files this definition was read from, named by path (rooms/, kits/, styles/, faults/, groupings/, proportions/ or partis/ records; build/ scripts; massings/catalog.json; elements/slots.json; mcp_server/core.py; a schema/ file; VISION.md, README.md or a top-level docs/ page), with at least one passage of twenty-five characters or more quoted verbatim in double quotes. The checker finds each quotation in the file it names and refuses the record if one is missing. docs/open-questions.md is generated and no glossary/ file may be a basis.

sense.description: Which sense this is, in a few words. Mandatory on BOTH records whenever this record's `term` or an `aka` collides, case-insensitively, with another record's; the two must then name each other in `confusable_with`.

aka.description: Other words for the same sense. Each joins the homonym check and the search haystack, so an aka that collides with another record's term needs a `sense` on both, exactly as a colliding term does.

order.description: Position within the family. Required on a record that `binds`, where it must equal the bound value's index in its schema enum; recommended elsewhere.

analogy.description: One sentence, where one is apt: at most thirty words, no digits.

more.description: A longer paragraph shown only on the term's own page, never in a popover. The same hygiene as the definition.

binds.description: Ties this word to a real value of a schema enum, so a screen that shows the value can show its definition. The seven fields that may be bound, their schemas and pointers are a closed table in build/check_glossary.py; a field is bound completely or not at all, and each value by exactly one record.

confusable_with.description: Ids of records a reader could mistake this one for. Symmetric: every id named must exist and must name this record back. Required between records whose strings collide.

see.description: Citations in the workbench's grammar (`kind:id`), each checked: `term:<id>` against the glossary itself, `brief:<id>` against briefs/, every other kind through the server's own citation validator.

surface.description: Only on families `surface` and `section`: what a page head says about the page it heads.

what.description: The page head's one line: at most thirty words.

read.description: The folded "how to read this page" list: each item at most thirty words.

try.description: One citation shown as a link, checked exactly as a `see` item is.

who.description: The reader, named as VISION.md names them.

line.description: What changes for that reader: at most forty-five words.

readers.description: Only on `about-tdl`: who the corpus is for, from VISION.md's own account.

is_not.description: Only on `about-tdl`: what the corpus is not, from VISION.md's own account, each at most thirty words.

bind.description: One enum value this record names. `schema` and `pointer` must equal the closed table's row for `field`, the pointer must reach an `enum` in that schema, and `value` must be one of its members.
